title: Explain RMS metrics showing zero after sort cycle by confirming metrics are scoped to sort GUID and reset on sort cycle
summary: When a sort cycle runs, the system sends a “reset metrics” bit/message, resets Tipper metrics, and triggers an API flow that generates a new sort GUID. Because RMS statistics are tied to the sort GUID, the new GUID causes the RMS tables/statistics to show no data (appearing zeroed out) for the new sort.
when_to_use: Use when RMS totals/metrics appear missing or zeroed out after a sort cycle, and you need to explain the behavior based on sort-cycle reset and sort GUID scoping.
not_for: Do not use this procedure to troubleshoot cases where metrics are zeroed out but there is no evidence that a sort-cycle reset/new sort GUID occurred; the source only provides the sort GUID reset explanation.
roles_and_responsibilities: L2_support: Interpret RMS zeroed-out totals as expected behavior when a sort cycle resets metrics and generates a new sort GUID; validate the discrepancy using the source’s described time-based metrics validation approach.
access_or_tools_needed: RMS metrics display (to observe zeroed-out totals/metrics).
Access to the system/API/database view used to confirm sort GUID generation (the source mentions an API call and sort GUID but does not name the exact tool surface).

system_preconditions: A sort cycle has occurred (so a reset metrics bit/message could have been sent and a new sort GUID could have been generated).

visual_references.description: Overall System RMS page description and transcript excerpt explaining: stats reset for each sort, reset metrics bit, Todd resets Tipper metrics, API call generates a new sort GUID, and statistics tied to sort GUID show no data/zeroed out after reset.

steps.title: Confirm RMS totals/metrics are expected to reset on each sort cycle
steps.purpose: Establish the source-described mechanism for why RMS totals may appear zeroed out after a sort cycle.
steps.instruction: When RMS totals/metrics appear missing or zeroed out after a sort cycle, apply the source’s described behavior: the sort cycle sends a bit/message indicating “reset metrics,” which resets Tipper metrics as part of the cycle.
steps.expected_result: You can explain that the observed zeroed-out RMS totals/metrics align with a sort-cycle “reset metrics” behavior rather than an independent data corruption issue.
steps.healthy_condition: RMS metrics are zeroed out immediately after a sort cycle in a way that matches the source’s described reset behavior (no totals anywhere for the new sort context).
steps.failure_condition: RMS metrics are zeroed out, but you cannot support that a sort-cycle reset occurred (no evidence of reset metrics/new sort GUID in the available evidence).

actions.label: Observe RMS totals/metrics after sort cycle
actions.exact_action: Observe the RMS metrics/totals display showing missing or zeroed-out values after the sort cycle.

stop_or_escalate_if: If metrics are zeroed out but there is no evidence of a sort-cycle reset/new sort GUID, stop and escalate for deeper investigation.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: When they cycle sort, they send a bit that says reset metrics... resets the Tipper metrics...

steps.title: Verify a new sort GUID was generated as part of the reset process
steps.purpose: Tie the zeroed-out RMS view to the source’s stated cause: new sort GUID generation during the reset flow.
steps.instruction: Confirm that the reset process included an API call that generated a new sort GUID (the source states this happens as part of the reset metrics flow). Use whatever system/API/database view you have available to confirm sort GUID generation; the source does not name the exact surface.
steps.expected_result: You determine that a new sort GUID was generated for the current sort cycle, explaining why RMS statistics for the new GUID show no data.
steps.healthy_condition: The evidence you can access indicates the sort GUID changed as part of the reset metrics flow.
steps.failure_condition: You cannot confirm that a new sort GUID was generated for the sort cycle in question.

actions.label: Confirm sort GUID generation
actions.exact_action: Confirm that the reset metrics flow includes an API call that generates a new sort GUID.

stop_or_escalate_if: If you cannot find evidence of a new sort GUID generation tied to the sort cycle, stop and escalate for deeper investigation.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: Then it's an API call... it generates a new sort GUID.

steps.title: Interpret the RMS result using sort GUID scoping (new GUID => no data/zeroed totals)
steps.purpose: Provide the correct interpretation of zeroed-out RMS totals based on the source’s rule for how statistics are stored/displayed.
steps.instruction: Use the source’s rule: every statistic is tied to a sort GUID. After you reset the sort GUID, the system looks at the tables and shows no data—so the RMS totals appear zeroed out for the new sort GUID.
steps.expected_result: You can state that the zeroed-out RMS totals are expected because statistics are scoped to the current sort GUID, and the new GUID has no prior rows yet (so tables show no data).
steps.healthy_condition: The RMS display shows no totals/data for the current sort context immediately after the sort GUID reset, consistent with “shows no data... all zeroed out.”
steps.failure_condition: RMS totals are zeroed out even though the sort GUID scoping/reset explanation does not fit the evidence (e.g., no reset/new GUID, or evidence contradicts the scoping behavior).

actions.label: Apply sort GUID scoping rule to RMS totals
actions.exact_action: Interpret RMS totals as tied to sort GUID; after resetting sort GUID, tables show no data (zeroed out).

stop_or_escalate_if: If the evidence does not support sort GUID reset/new GUID, stop and escalate for deeper investigation.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: Every statistic on my end is a tied to a sort GUID... So you reset the sort GUID, it looks at the tables and shows no data. So it's all zeroed out.

steps.title: Validate the metrics discrepancy using the source’s time-based approach (if needed)
steps.purpose: When you need additional confirmation beyond the conceptual explanation, use the source’s described validation method.
steps.instruction: If needed for validation, pick a specific time and determine what the metrics “should have been showing,” then work through the discrepancy between expected vs observed values using the source’s described approach.
steps.expected_result: You can reconcile the observed zeroed-out totals with what the metrics should have shown at a specific time, based on the source’s validation approach.
steps.healthy_condition: Your time-based expected-vs-observed reasoning matches the sort-cycle reset/new sort GUID behavior.
steps.failure_condition: Time-based validation cannot be reconciled with the sort-cycle reset/new sort GUID explanation.

healthy_conditions: RMS totals/metrics show no data/zeroed-out values for the current sort context immediately after sort-cycle reset, consistent with statistics being tied to sort GUID.
